Private Tombstone and Bisbee Day Tour from Phoenix

Scottsdale Sprinters runs a private Tombstone and Bisbee tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale as one vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 12-hour day: the group is driven south, waited on at every confirmed stop, and driven home. The published window is 10-12 hours and it bills 10 of them, so the day starts at $1,250 in the Luxury SUV (Suburban) and the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,450 before 8% tax — roughly $104 a seat with 14 aboard. Below: the row's own 10 steps, why this page prints no mileage, which vehicle fits, and how the quote is built. Reservations: (623) 986-6339.

Last updated: September 18, 2026

What is a private Tombstone and Bisbee tour from Phoenix and Scottsdale?

It is the whole vehicle and one chauffeur held for a 12-hour day to two southern Arizona towns and back, not a seat on somebody else's coach. 6 vehicles are offered for it: the day starts at $1,250 in the smallest cabin and tops out at $2,950, every figure quoted in writing first. Scottsdale Sprinters sells the transport around whatever you choose to do down there, never the attractions themselves. Your group decides who is aboard and how the booked hours are spent; the chauffeur drives, parks, waits, and brings everyone home. Per head the arithmetic is plainer than it looks. The 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter splits $1,450 across its seats, about $104 each; the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax) splits $2,250 across 29, about $78. Those are the current published hourly rates carried across this day, never a fare per person, and admission is separate.

How does the day work, from pickup to the drive home?

The tour publishes 10 steps and states the window as 10-12 hours, and the row writes 1 of them as conditional rather than promised — the move between the two towns — because it depends on what the confirmed stops actually take. That is the row's own list, word for word, and the conditional step is printed in full above: "Continue to Bisbee if it fits the confirmed service window". Nothing on this page turns it into a promise, and nothing quietly drops it from a quote. Everything else hangs off times you have already confirmed with whoever runs each stop: "Early morning pickup" is set backward from the first of them, and "Return to Scottsdale" closes the row because the vehicle is yours for the whole window. Which vehicle fits the group, and what does the day cost?

Group size decides it. This tour offers 6 vehicles, and every row below prices the identical 12-hour day: the published hourly rate times 10 billable hours, because 12 requested hours earn 2 free hours on the standard ladder, against each vehicle's own 4-hour minimum. Up to 6 travellers the Luxury SUV (Suburban) runs the day for $1,250. The Executive Black Sprinter and Executive White Sprinter share a rate at $145 an hour and seat 14 each. The Maybach Jet Sprinter leads the row's own list at $295 an hour, the dearest line in this table at $2,950; past 14 seats it is the Mini Bus (24 Pax) and the Executive Mini Coach (29 Pax). The per-seat column divides the day total by seated capacity — friends splitting one fare. It is why the cheapest seat and the cheapest day are different vehicles: the Luxury SUV (Suburban) is the least expensive booking at $1,250, while the Mini Bus (24 Pax) carries the cheapest seat at $77. What is in the fare, and what is not?

A 12-hour day in the 14-seat Executive Black Sprinter is $1,450 before 8% tax — $145 an hour across 10 billable hours, roughly $104 a seat split 14 ways. The least expensive vehicle on the list runs the same day for $1,250. Three rules build every number: the day is priced by the hour against each vehicle's published minimum, hours above the ladder's rungs earn free hours, and 8% tax is the only addition. 50% is taken today by card, the balance 48 hours before pickup. What the fare excludes is the part of the day that is not ours to sell: "No attraction admission or tour is included unless the written quote lists it. Use the City of Tombstone and City of Bisbee visitor resources to choose current stops, reserve any timed experience directly, and send the confirmed address and check-in time for transportation review." Lunch is a stop rather than a service — "No eating or food inside the vehicle. Drinks are fine; snacks wait for the next stop."

How far is it, and how should the day be timed?

This page publishes no mileage and no drive time, and that is deliberate: not 1 service-area guide in this repo states a distance to either town, so stating one here would be inventing it. The row answers the question itself, and its answer is reprinted whole below. In the tour's own words: "This is a long southern-Arizona route. Final timing depends on the exact pickup, confirmed Tombstone and Bisbee stops, road conditions, breaks, and the return plan." So the confirmed times do the planning. Send the stops you have reserved and the check-in each one gave you, and the pickup is set backward from the earliest of them; the 10-12 hours band on the booking card is what the row publishes, and the written quote names the window your date actually gets.

Do both towns really fit into one day?

Sometimes, and the row refuses to pretend otherwise — which is why 1 of its 10 steps is written as a condition rather than a plan. What decides it is how long your confirmed stops run, not how fast anyone drives. The step reads "Continue to Bisbee if it fits the confirmed service window", and the phrase that matters is "the confirmed service window": the booked hours are a fixed quantity, and every timed thing you reserve spends some of them. So book the second town as an intention and confirm it as a fact. Reserve what you want, send the confirmations, and the desk says in writing whether they fit the window you are buying — or quotes a longer one.

What does the tour actually publish as the day out?

The row names 6 highlights, and they are the only ones this page will name: OK Corral gunfight show, Tombstone historic district, Bisbee Copper Queen Mine tour, Bisbee art galleries, Boot Hill Graveyard, Historic saloons. Each is somewhere the vehicle can wait while the group is out of it, which is the whole point of the booking. Two of them are timed experiences somebody else runs, and the row is explicit about who controls them: "The mine operator controls tour format, availability, check-in, age and accessibility rules, and conditions. Reserve directly with the operator, then send the confirmed check-in location and time for route review." Reserve those first: they are the fixed points the day is built around. The rest are places you walk into and out of at your own pace. The official bodies behind both towns are cited below; this page lifts no hour, fee or timetable from them.

Who is this day for, and what should we bring?

Groups — and that is as far as this page will go, because the row names no audience. The only honest description is the shape of the booking: 1 vehicle, 1 chauffeur, 12 hours, and a party between 6 and 29 people. On whether it suits families the row sends you to the people who set the rules, and so does this page: "Review each attraction's current age, accessibility, and safety policies directly before booking. Add the confirmed stops and times to the transportation request." Age limits and what an experience expects of a visitor are theirs to publish. Bags have a published cap per vehicle rather than a house rule: the Maybach Jet Sprinter takes 4, the Executive Black Sprinter 40, and the 1 unit without an owner-confirmed number has its fit confirmed in writing instead of guessed. Coats and camera kit stay aboard between stops. The chauffeur is a resource: "Ask your chauffeur for anything. Stops, temperature, volume, a photo. Really."

Where can the day start, and how is it quoted?

Pickup is a street address in any of the 10 metro cities with a published service-area page, not a zone or a depot. Reserving takes 3 things — the date, the number of people and one address — plus the confirmations for anything you have already reserved. The published service areas are Scottsdale, Phoenix, Paradise Valley, Tempe, Mesa, Chandler, Gilbert, Glendale, Cave Creek and San Tan Valley. One pickup address for the whole party keeps a group together at the start of a day that begins early. Every figure here is today's published table; the quote you act on is the written one, naming the vehicle, the hours, the 8% tax and the 50% deposit. Call Scottsdale Sprinters on (623) 986-6339, or send those 3 things and request a current quote.
